- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast shows gradual upward bias (slight upward drift) but fails to capture sharp downward spikes in true outcomes.
- When true prices spike upward (e.g., 85+), model fails to overshoot and instead lags behind, underestimating the peak.
- After a spike, model tends to overcorrect downward, often overshooting the true mean by 1–2 points before stabilizing.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: it overcorrects after sharp declines, then slowly drifts back up, missing the true trend.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation, especially in the first 10–15 days, suggesting lag in capturing recent volatility.
- Model fails to account for sudden drops in true prices (e.g., 70–75 range) — often underestimates them by 2–5 points.
- When true prices are near or below 75, model tends to underestimate further, showing a downward bias in low-price regimes.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven volatility (e.g., auction dates, regulatory changes) — leading to persistent bias in mid-to-late forecast.
- Forecast shows no adaptive response to recent true price volatility — remains flat or slowly increasing, despite sharp true price movements.
